answer: The knoll multiplier is published, charged in sonnet, and ivory lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4371 identities would post 3713 proofs and burn roughly 77 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
